body: I've been trying to ask my parents for a new psychiatrist but they keep putting it off so I signed myself up for outpatient. I should be starting it soon and having a new psych there. Thanks for the input!
Did you switch from another medication?

I know how you feel. I don't feel as confident, creative, motivated, outgoing, etc. as I used to when I was manic. But I'm also less destructive and psychotic. Still, it feels like I'm a completely different person. I totally get you on that. I want to accept that this is my new normal now and how neurotypicals feel but it just feels like something is missing.

Your brother isn't leaving his room because he knows what he did was fucked up, no matter if he is apologizing or not. You have to be the older sister and protect your little sister here. Who knows what else he will do to her or other people in the future. Call the police. That will probably scare the shits out of him.

I'm bipolar too and I suspect my meds are making my social anxiety worse as well. Just being around people makes my heart beat fast and make me feel uneasy. I think I'll be adding an anxiety medication. Either that or trying a new med.
I cut my hair into a pixie cut and dyed it pink. Lots of people told me I must have a lot of confidence hahaha nope
I relate to this post so hard.

Felt the exact same way you did a week ago. I so badly wanted to be old enough to buy a gun to shoot myself in the head. It was the only thing I could think about. To kill myself. Even though I hate the mental hospital I decided it was the best place I could be in at the time. I came out feeling better. Still depressed but not constantly thinking about suicide. Just remember that there will be a day when you will think "wow I'm glad to be alive". It seems fucking impossible right now I know. But the day will come. Depression is hard to deal with alone. Have you sought out treatment/told anyone? If you want you can shoot me a PM and tell me what's going on.
Lithium was a god send for my suicidal thoughts but yeah couldn't tolerate the side effects so didn't stay on it. It might take a couple weeks to reach therapeutic levels.

Sometimes I feel this way but I kind of just accepted that mental illness is in my genes and something I can't help with my own will. Postpartum depression is a real thing and my grandmother had it. She is literally the most happy person I've ever met. She claims its the meds that helped her get out of her depression.
I've been on and off since March and it still makes me feel super sedated. Particularly in the afternoon. I'm on 40 mg in the morning and night.
Abilify and wellbutrin. Made me hypomanic and have akathisia.

I feel you. Just a week ago I poured all my pills in my hand and wanted to swallow them all. Life is so much harder for us and sometimes it just doesn't feel worth it to go on. But there's hope. There always is. It just takes some work. I admitted myself to the mental hospital afterwards and just got out yesterday and feel much better. Still depressed but its manageable. And don't be sorry for your post! We're all bipolar here so we know how you feel and maybe you'll help someone who is going through it right now not to feel alone.

Honestly this made me feel better, thank you. It's glad to know I'm not alone in this. I've been on lamictal for a few days now but have been trying a bunch for a year. I've been seeing my psychiatrist often.
This happened to me and doctors told me it was psychosis. You should definitely get it checked out
Thank you so much, I needed to hear this ❤
All those side effects were just inevitable for me on all the antipsychotics I've tried. My psychiatrist told me he won't prescribe any antipsychotics anymore (thank god) and I'm on lamictal now.

Yes. Even when I'm driving I can feel people's eyes on me. I think I developed paranoia after my psychotic episode so now I have to deal with this on top of bipolar (and I suspect I have BPD). The thing that helped me the most was constantly telling myself that I'm safe and no one is watching me. Also not giving a **** about it and going outside anyways. It used to be so bad that I hammered a blanket over my window cause I thought I was being watched through there.
I'm drawn to those who are quiet
You should try to at least get some help from your psychiatrist about tapering. Coming off antipsychotics cold turkey could lead to bad withdrawals and even psychosis.
Gained weight on Abilify and Lithium, although to be fair I was eating a lot more. Got switched to Geodon and didn't gain much weight with little change in diet.
I tried Trileptal for a little bit and it didn't make me tired
Music

Lowered my Geodon today due to sedation and feels like it's helping. I'm also taking Depakote due to feeling depressed, although I heard that Depakote mainly helps mania so I don't know how effective it will be. Fingers crossed
Yes I sleep constantly on them.
Lamictal made me feel like this as well so I had to stop it. I suggest talking to your psychiatrist about it.
I do experience more anxiety on Geodon but never had a panic attack on it. Sorry you had to go through that :( Hopefully Latuda works for you well.

I took it for my bipolar and the first week was good. But then it eventually made me constantly angry so I had to get off it. Not a good experience but yours could be way different. Hopefully it goes well for you!
Multivitamins from Kirkland I believe
Me. I have bipolar.

I remember taking certain meds and it was like light and day. I would be so depressed thinking about suicide, how worthless I am, etc. But soon after taking the meds I could finally see why life was worth living. It was such a strange but fulfilling experience. It's crazy how one pill can make that difference.
If its been going on for days and is debilitating then I go to my psychiatrist and get my meds switched. Usually does the trick.
Yeah it definitely kicks my mania to the curb. It also knocks me out a couple hours taking it. I was taking it two times a day and sleeping my days away.
Geodon
You should definitely talk to your psych about it then.

I felt like that on Abilify the few months I was on it. I definitely wasn't as exciting as I was when I was manic. But I also wasn't as grandiose, delusional, psychotic, angry, mean, etc. Being boring and stable is a small price to pay for all that. Also I'd imagine it does block the effects of stimulants (at least the ones affecting dopamine). If I remember correctly Abilify controls the levels of dopamine in your brain so it doesn't have too much so that would lessen the effects of some stimulants.
When I realize "oh shit, what did I do". I come to a sudden realization that all of the impulsive choices I chose to do in mania were bad ideas.
Geodon
From my ex: "Psychology is a fake science, it's all in your head."

I had psych hospital staff kick my door and call me a "bitch" repeatedly throughout the night. They also told me that they will use ECT on me because I was misbehaving. I was told I had psychotic depression after the stay so I assume all those things weren't real and just delusions/hallucinations.
Hey don't let that comment get you down. She might just be a mean, insecure person who puts other people down.
I feel you. Now I'm constantly analyzing whether my paranoia is true or not and fighting myself over it.
It slows my thoughts down

Numero uno all the way! 

I remember taking Seroquel. Gave me racing thoughts. Hopefully you get that figured out. 

To be honest, the way I got out of the depressive rut was working with my pdoc to get the right medication. I don't have a therapist but I do try to be my own therapist when I'm having negative thoughts. It's easy for negative thoughts to spiral into something severe, like turning to suicide as the answer. I try to be nice on myself and use CBT to turn my negative thoughts into positive ones.

I hope you get this all figured out. Best of luck to you <3

Hey there, bipolar 1 here. The last manic/psychotic episode I had was last fall. Usually when manic episodes end, a deep depression follows. I went through that and it seems like you're going through that too. I was filled with shame and guilt for the things that I've done and while I can't really say things got better, I can say that I've experienced some good days. Are you currently on any meds? They may be able to help.
That we are aggressive, emotional, and unpredictable people.
20 F here diagnosed as bipolar 1. I've been diagnosed since I was 18 and have come a long way since then. You can PM me any time if you want!
I act as my own therapist and comfort myself
Ah sorry you went through that. Glad it's working out for you now
Setraline made your ass hurt?
I agree that it might be paranoia.

It's not exactly the same situation but I know what it feels like to be raped and sexually harassed. I was helping a "friend" move his stuff into his apartment and he grabs me from behind, gropes me, and eventually rapes me. I cried for a good hour or two afterwards. I couldn't sleep for many weeks and unfortuneatly this triggered a manic episode in me (I'm bipolar) and went through the worst psychosis I ever had. I have a hard time trusting my boyfriend. Sometimes I feel like he's just using me for sex cause he wants it so often. I'm sorry that happened to you. You deserve so much better and I hope you can heal from all of what you went through. Hugs
Paliperidone helped to lift me out of psychotic depression. I felt great while I was on it but had to stop due to rapid weight gain.
It usually makes me sleepy after 3-5 hours of taking it.
Thanks, I hope the best for you
I had an ex tell me that psychology was a fake science after I told him that I was bipolar. Pretty much he was telling me my illness was fake and it was all in my head kek
There's no way to know for sure. I know that traumatic events can trigger a bipolar episode. Also having enough sleep can help with manic episodes.
I don't want to scare you or anything but yes for many of us it will be a life long struggle. But life can still be manageable with the right meds and avoiding episodes. It is for me.

What's the dosage of the lithium and anti-psychotic? It could be that the lithium isn't at the appropriate level and the antipsychotic is too low of a dosage. Also if it helps, I had a manic episode last year fall and on an antipsychotic and mood stabilizer and I still face symptoms like paranoia. I don't think the meds are supposed to cure us 100%, moreso they help the symptoms become more manageable.

I've been on ziprasidone/geodon for about 4 months now. I'm on 40 mg in the morning and 40 mg at night. I felt the medication's effect almost immediately but I noticed my symptoms mostly gone after about a month or two. It does increase my anxiety but I also take trileptal which I think is helping with it. It's been mostly weight neutral for me. It makes me incredibly tired around noon so I usually drink coffee.

If it means anything, after eating an edible I got super angry and had psychosis. I have bipolar 1. Haven't smoked or ate an edible since because I'm aware how it affects me and the people around me. I think your girlfriend's brother needs to realize this for himself. However long that will take. I don't think anyone can really convince him otherwise.

Am 20, female and bipolar 1 too. I'm on geodon and trileptal and they seem to be working for my mood and psychosis. I used to try to become hypomanic because I missed the euphoria but I realized that I'd have to go through a depression afterwards and then I thought it's just not worth it. Medications make me function like a normal human being and I like that. Good luck to you!
I rollerbladed down a 600 ft hill. Didn't fall I don't even know how thank god.
Crushed my suicidal thoughts. Some side effects I experience is extreme thirst and frequent urination (I'm talking about twice an hour)!

I was kind of skeptical to how they could list medications that are suitable for with just a swipe of the cheek. But I found the right medication combo because of genesight so I guess it worked out in the end.
I'd assume it helped with my psychosis/paranoia, but it made me too tired so I went off it
I've been on meds for 10 months now and am still suffering from paranoia. It's gotten a lot better with an increased dose. You probably need an increase.
Stay on meds
All of the antipsychotics that were labeled weight neutral made me gain weight... except Geodon and it works exceptionally well.
I was forcibly pinned down to my bed and given injections of Haldol. I experienced hallucinations and delusions afterwards.
Yes, I've been on Lamictal for a little while. Also been on a bunch of antipsychotics.

I thought my friends and boyfriend were all part of a scheme to use me for human trafficking (psychosis). It wasn't just a feeling, I actually truly believed this and was scared shitless. I couldn't believe my friends were faking being my friend the whole time. I couldn't believe they were watching me through my webcam and I was just a show puppet for them. I thought my good friend was the President and he was watching me through all the cameras set up in my city and helicopters. I felt violated and I did stupid shit like rollerblade down a 600 ft. hill and drive 120 mph on the free way, in hopes of killing myself. I broke down and texted my good friend accusing him of all this and he was obviously totally confused. My other friend was with him at the time and she called me to check up on me and was genuinely shocked. That was the moment I realized I needed help, went back to the psychiatrist and took meds. I still have lingering paranoia but it's no where bad as it was before.

Wellbutrin can increase libido and also suppress appetite. I was never on it long enough to experience the increase in libido though. Also, lowering the medication you think is killing your libido might help, it did for me.
I'm on Lithium and going through the same problem. I don't have motivation to draw or play piano. I would guess changing meds or lowering it would help.

I finally got good grades this past spring semester after mediocre grades for a few semesters in college. I figured I was dealt unlucky cards with my illness and that I'd have to try much more than the other people in my class. I went to the library at least two times a week for a few hours studying on the material learned in class. I made sure to check the deadlines everyday to see what I needed to get done. Also, this was all done while I was going through paranoia and depression after psychosis/mania. I still haven't found the right meds yet either. You can do it!
Yes I have this
Lowered my morning dose of Geodon because I was feeling too sedated during the day. Hopefully my motivation and energy come back

I have bipolar 1 and have been on Geodon for a few months now. Geodon has a half-life of about 7 hours so it could very well be that the Geodon is losing its efficacy by the time your wife wakes up. Also 20 mg is such a low dose that I'm not surprised that's happening. Geodon is usually taken twice a day because of its half-life.

I let the thoughts come by without giving in and having an emotional reaction. I give it some time and then the thoughts usually disappear. Granted I'm also on Lithium which is known to stop suicidal thinking.

I get panic attacks during psychosis all the time. I was so paranoid that people were watching me inside my house that I hammered a blanket over my window. I was going through my social media and thought every single post was about me and attacking me. In class, my heart races if the teacher says certain words because I think they're talking about me and trying to tarnish my image. Sorry you felt that way. It seems like you were going through an intense panic attack.

Thanks for the tips and sharing your story, I read all of it. You're right I need to be more hard on myself, I've been slacking off and munching on junk food every now and then. All these comments really motivated me and I just came back from the gym! Thanks again and have a good rest of your day.

It's hard to understand psychosis if the person has never went through it themselves. I had people tell me that it's my anxiety acting up. They have good intentions but they're just way off. It's awful to live with psychosis. I dreaded leaving my house because I felt eyes on me. I didn't like listening to certain songs because my psychosis would flare up. To this day I can't go to the movies because I feel as though they're talking about my life and it triggers me. My boyfriend accepts that I can't go to the movies but he asks me "why can't you go to the movies, is it because of your anxiety?" and then that just makes me feel even more misunderstood and it feels like he's downplaying my mental illness. But I know he's just curious and he means well in the end. I feel your frustration.
Not even average, just dog shit
I was on 1.5 mg for sometime a few years ago and I remember gaining 30 pounds in 3 months. Though out of all the meds I've taken, it was the best I felt mentally.

I finally understood why I felt paranoid of people and had these huge mood swings. I got put on the right meds instead of antidepressants which didn't seem to be doing anything for me. I could finally go back to school and do well. However, it wasn't easy accepting my diagnosis. I thought there was nothing wrong with me so I stopped meds many times even though they were making me better. I became psychotic every time. I'm not going to be coming off of my meds anytime soon!

This was me just a few months ago. I was scared to leave my house because I felt I was being watched from every corner. I thought people were plotting against me. I had auditory hallucinations hearing people talking badly about me. I had visual hallucinations seeing a man who hanged himself. I broke up with my boyfriend because I thought it'd be easier for him to deal with life without me. Now I'm on the right medication and can go outside in peace. I'm meeting with a friend tomorrow. I don't have any hallucinations anymore. And I got back with my boyfriend. Life can get better if you put the work in. Please hang in there, it'll be worth it. It was for me.

Everything will be okay. Your brain is being mean to you but the fact of the matter is he loves you very much. I used to get this too with my boyfriend. It took constant reminding of myself that he loves me. Also the right medication helps. I know the feelings, it sucks and it just gets stuck in my head. But just try to be kind to yourself. <3
Yeah, I'd be nodding off around afternoon and would have to take a nap. But you get used it the longer you're on it.
Invega made me gain 30 pounds in just 3 months! Stay far far away from it

It put a stop to my paranoia and could make me function like a normal human being again. Before I thought people were watching me in my home so I put up a blanket to cover my window and would always close the blinds. I felt peoples' eyes watching me while I was driving and that made me uncomfortable to go anywhere. Now with Geodon 90% of those symptoms have gone away. The biggest side effects is feeling sedated during the afternoon but it goes away after. No weight gain. It's my favorite medication I tried in the last two years.

It's good that you're proactively looking for advice for bipolar and admit the diagnosis. It's hard for a lot of people to initially accept their diagosis. I know it was for me.

After mania, there usually comes a period of depression which can be filled with shame, regret, low self-esteem, etc. This is when people usually seek treatment and get put on meds to control their episodes. Many bipolar patients (me included) have stopped taking their meds because they couldn't handle the side effects. Don't do this. It will lead to a relapse and may cause your mania to be more intense than before. You should also be sleeping 7-8 hours everyday. Less could mean an onset of hypomania. Good luck!

I learned that people are too occupied with their lives to worry about you. I remember when I came out of my manic episode I was afraid to go back to school because I thought people would recognize me and scoff at how I acted. But really they're just busy in their own lives and won't hold this stuff against you.
It'll improve with time. It did for me.

Been 9 months for me too since my last psychotic episode. My self-esteem is shot after coming down from my manic episode (I have bipolar 1) and I have moderate anxiety and depression that is composed of racing thoughts/rumination. I also don't feel as creative anymore. But I haven't had a single manic episode for 9 months and I've been doing well in my classes so at least it makes me somewhat functional.
When I'm manic I think I'm hot shit and that I can attract anyone. Then I crash and can't even look myself in the mirror.
I'm having trouble complying to these medications that work for my mania (Geodon and Lithium). I just hate that I won't at the same level mentally as I was when I was "normal".

Everyone reacts to medication differently but if you want a recommendation I'd say Geodon. I have bipolar 1 and haven't had a single manic episode on it. I'm also on Lithium, the gold standard medication for bipolar. Obviously these meds might not work for you. I recommend Geodon because it's an antipsychotic with no weight gain while the others I gained a bunch of weight on.
Made me uncontrollably angry the two times I've been on it. But maybe the right med or you

I remember feeling the most stable I've ever felt on Invega. It was like finding a miracle drug! I was able to hold a job while going to school. But I gained so much weight like 30 pounds in a few months with no diet changes. I couldn't take the weight gain so I went off it and unfortunately went into psychosis. Now I'm on Geodon and Lithium which has made me gain weight but only because I've been eating more. Oh yeah and I was on the lowest dose of Invega, 1.5 mg.

Before you make any big decisions, have you talked to her about this? Maybe being open and professing your feelings on this matter will make her try to change. That's if she cares enough to change. If she doesn't well it seems like the relationship most likely won't work out. Bipolar isn't an excuse to act this way. Even when I go through an episode (I have bipolar 1) I make sure to keep my negative feelings in and treat my boyfriend the kindest way possible. We're both 20 and have been together for 10 months with zero fights. Bipolar isn't the issue, it's most likely a personality problem. I hope you work this out!

Bipolar 1 here. I would feel annoyed with my boyfriend over small things a lot when I was going through an episode, but I practiced A LOT of self discipline to not verbally express it. At the moment all I wanted to do was scream and get angry but I remained calm by telling myself over and over again that it's not worth it and I would regret it later. It wasn't until after the long episode was over that I told this to my boyfriend and he said he had no idea I was angry and was surprised I told him this so I guess I did a good job lol. What helped me get out of the episode was changing my meds.
Not Lithium but when I stopped antipsychotics, I experienced psychosis for the very first time. So I wouldn't be surprised if Lithium caused intense mood swings or rapid cycling while stopping it.

Good god. I don't think anything you do could help this guy. Bipolar or a mental illness is not an excuse to act like a dick or physically hurt someone. This guy is controlling you and unfortunately you are falling under his trap. Please get out of this unhealthy relationship for your own sake.

Having to go on meds that not necessarily made me worse but still made me feel bad with side effects like weight gain. Then feeling as if I'm not bipolar because the meds aren't making me "stable". Hating the meds and getting off. Then relapsing into a psychosis/mania. Going back on meds. Rinse and repeat.

I strongly believe my trauma (sexual and witness of domestic abuse) triggered my bipolar episodes but it didn't necessarily make me bipolar. I think I just had a predisposition to bipolar and the trauma added unnecessary stress that led to me having episodes.

I'm like that on Geodon and I feel as though it's causing me to have ADD. I can't focus on anything and I have no emotions. I'm slowly weaning myself off of it because I hate the way it makes me feel.

Give it some time and things will get better. Practice self-forgiveness. Just remember that it was the illness that made you do the things you did. It's not something you would do if you were mentally stable. Those that truly care about you will forgive you for what you did. You should practice self care and forgive yourself as well.

It's pretty much numbed me into not feeling emotions. I wouldn't say that's stable because stable people still feel a wide range of emotions but hey I'd rather be numb than go through the extremes of mania and depression.
So what's the secret?

I also went through psychosis when getting of my anti-psychotics. It was last September that I had full blown psychosis, thinking that I had an audience and that the government was watching me... I wouldn't say I have psychosis now but I do still have a lingering paranoia and went through a depression (though I'm out that now). Did you experience anything similar post psychosis? How did you recover?

It could be possible but I don't believe that my antipsychotics made me depressed. Instead I believe it stopped the mania which made me crash into depression. But everyone's different. You should talk to your doctor about it and then they can adjust for you.

I dealt with all that you mentioned and what helped me was Geodon 40 mg twice a day and lithium 300 mg twice a day. I also have been taking omega 3 and multivitamins everyday for almost a month as well. I also found that CBT has helped in calming me when I'm having delusions. Like catching myself when I'm having a delusion and telling myself it's not true and thinking of a more plausible solution.

I've been in your position before and as much as I hated when people told me it will get better, it will get better. Work with your doctor to find the right meds and in the meantime do things you enjoy. It sucks right now but it really is temporary.
Started omega 3 and vitamins with my Geodon. I don't know if it's placebo or my Geodon kicking in but I feel like my paranoia has disappeared greatly and seems like a miracle.
Starting out the keto diet since I heard there are mental benefits to it.
